source_checks.finding: Page (fetched at a later offset) says: 'Swipe left on the message, tap [the Delete button], then tap Delete and Report Spam.' (exact words verified; the ref's excerpt 'Delete and Report Spam' matches). It says 'You can't report a message after you've replied to it.' For SMS, MMS, or RCS: 'If you don't see the option to report spam messages you receive with SMS, MMS, or RCS: Contact your carrier.' It also says 'Reporting spam doesn't prevent the sender from sending messages. To avoid receiving their messages, block the contact.' Applies to iPhone, the user's platform.

Distractor for Android Google Messages. The page gives the 'Touch and hold the conversation you want to report', then Block, Report spam, OK steps. It does not apply to this iPhone user and is correctly unused in the target.

required_actions.action: Swipe left on the unopened message, tap Delete, then tap Delete and Report Spam
Reporting is not possible after replying to the message
If the report option is not shown for SMS, MMS, or RCS, contact the carrier
Block the sender separately, since reporting does not stop their messages

source_checks.finding: Page says: 'From the conversation, tap More options', then Details, 'Block & report spam,' then OK (verified). Reported conversations go to the 'Spam & blocked' folder. To undo, mark the conversation as not spam. Reporting sends the spammer's phone number and the last 10 incoming messages to Google. Applies to Android with Google Messages, the user's platform.

Distractor for iPhone. The page says: 'Go to the conversation with the person you want to block, then tap the person's icon at the top.' 'Tap Info, scroll down, then tap Block Contact.' and 'You can't block a group conversation.' It does not apply to this Android user and is correctly unused in the target.

Page is titled 'How to Recognize and Report Spam Text Messages'. Verified wording: 'Copy the message and forward it to 7726 (SPAM).' and 'Report it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.' The ref's 'don't tap links in unexpected texts asking for personal or financial information' is supported in substance by the page's advice not to click on any links in such texts. Applies to any phone, the spam text the user describes.

required_actions.action: Do not tap any links in the text, since it asks for bank login details
Contact the bank using a phone number or website you know is real, if worried about the account
Open the conversation, tap More options, then Details
Tap Block & report spam, then OK
Reported conversations are moved to the Spam & blocked folder
Optionally forward the message to 7726 (SPAM) and report it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
